vocabulary.meaning: the set of words a person knows and uses
examples: A larger vocabulary makes reading easier.
Building vocabulary takes repeated exposure.

vocabulary.meaning: a learning method that reviews information at increasing intervals
examples: Spaced repetition can improve long-term memory.
Many vocabulary apps use spaced repetition.

vocabulary.meaning: a card or digital item with a question or word on one side and an answer on the other
examples: She uses flashcards to learn new words.
Digital flashcards are easy to review on the bus.

vocabulary.meaning: the ability to remember information without seeing the answer
examples: Active recall is more powerful than simply rereading a list.
The exercise tests your recall of yesterday's words.

vocabulary.meaning: to learn something so that you can remember it exactly
examples: He tries to memorise ten new words a day.
It is easier to memorise words when you use them in context.

vocabulary.meaning: the ability to keep information in memory over time
examples: Regular review improves retention.
Sleep also supports memory retention.

vocabulary.meaning: to study information again in order to remember it
examples: Review old vocabulary before adding too many new words.
A short daily review is more useful than one long session each month.

vocabulary.meaning: the sentence or situation around a word that helps explain its meaning
examples: Learn vocabulary in context rather than as isolated translations.
Context helps you choose the right meaning of a word.

vocabulary.meaning: how often something occurs or is used
examples: High-frequency words are useful to learn first.
Word frequency can help learners prioritise vocabulary.

vocabulary.meaning: a study method in which you try to produce an answer from memory
examples: Active recall makes your brain work harder than passive rereading.
Use active recall by covering the definition and testing yourself.
